reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows DTA on high-temperature alloys with calibration up to 2439 °C, supporting the feasibility of precise melting temperature and enthalpy measurements, but it does not address dilatometry, volume change, high-throughput screening, or the specific ±5–10% precision for HEAs. E2 describes low-to-moderate temperature DSC, not relevant to melting of HEAs. Thus, only the general DSC/DTA capability is partially supported, while the key premises on integrated dilatometry, high-throughput efficiency, and specific precision claims lack direct evidence.
premises: DSC can measure melting temperature, enthalpy, and entropy of fusion for HEAs with ±5 K and ±5–10% precision
In-situ calibrated dilatometry can measure volume change at melting for HEAs with ±5–10% precision
High-throughput DSC/dilatometry is efficient for screening various HEA compositions
Standard DSC on simpler alloys and prior DTA studies (E1) demonstrate similar accuracies
Rigorous in-situ calibration using high-temperature reference points mitigates calibration drift and integration uncertainties
